body: The best-known systems are explicitly "techno-fundamental": fundamentals (EPS/sales growth, ROE, catalysts) pick *what* to buy; Stage 2/Trend Template and pivots decide *when*; and the stop decides *how much*. A practical rule: only buy fundamentally strong stocks when they are in Stage 2, and ignore (or exit) fundamentally strong stocks in Stage 4.
title: technical_trading_risk › Takeaway

body: Lynch's edge was industrial-scale legwork: hundreds of company visits and hundreds of annual reports a year, 13-hour days, Saturdays, a week a month on the road, with very high early turnover and extreme diversification once the fund grew. Underneath was a small starting base ($18–22M) and a then-unusual Fidelity freedom to visit any company. The "average Magellan investor lost money" claim is an unsourced myth. The accurate version is that investors' dollar-weighted returns lagged the fund's time-weighted return, roughly 13–17% vs. 22–29%, depending on period and method.
title: buffett_lynch › Takeaway

body:
- **Fisher**, *Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits* (1958), ch. 2 "What Scuttlebutt Can Do": the business grapevine (competitors, customers, suppliers, ex-employees, research people, trade-association staff) gives an accurate picture of each company's relative strengths in an industry, built from a representative *cross-section* of opinions. It is a cross-section, not one tip. ([elearnmarkets summary](https://elearnmarkets.com/school/units/common-stocks-and-uncommon-profits/what-scuttlebutt-can-do), [TIP summary](https://www.theinvestorspodcast.com/billionaire-book-club-executive-summary/common-stocks-and-uncommon-profits/))
- **Buffett / American Express (1964)**: after the Nov-1963 salad-oil fraud (Allied Crude / De Angelis; about $150M of "collateral oil" was mostly seawater), Buffett spent an evening with the cashier at Ross's Steak House in Omaha, checking whether diners still used Amex cards. He also checked banks and stores on traveler's cheques. He concluded the franchise was intact and put about 40% of the partnership (~$13M) into the stock during 1964. ([Fortune 2012](https://fortune.com/2012/11/21/why-warren-buffetts-betting-big-on-american-express), [Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2017/05/27/1-stock-that-was-pivotal-in-billionaire-warren-buf.aspx)) Lesson: scuttlebutt answers *one decisive question* (is the moat damaged?), not "what will next quarter's EPS be".
- **Lynch**, *One Up on Wall Street*: invest in what you see first as a customer (the Hanes L'eggs story); pass the "two-minute drill" (category, why it will grow, what must go right, what could go wrong). ([SuperSummary](https://supersummary.com/one-up-on-wall-street/part-2-chapters-11-15-summary), [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Up_on_Wall_Street))

body:
| Date | What management said | What the numbers show (screener) |
|---|---|---|
| 30-Apr-2025 (volunteered, opening remarks) | "Working capital days also improved with inventory and debtor days sharply reducing." "Cash flow and working capital are expected to improve considerably going forward." | FY25 receivables INR 701 cr, debtor days 55 |
| 31-Jul-25, 07-Nov-25, 29-Jan-26 | No mention of debtors; credit given to "better working capital management" for the lower finance cost | (no half-year receivables data checked) |
| 28-Apr-2026 (only after an analyst asked; the opening remarks spoke of "stronger cash generation") | "None of them are sticky debtors." INR 260 cr "due to a technical reason" arrived on 1-2 April. Q4 domestic revenue was up ~45%, and domestic customers pay more slowly. GST inflates the number. "Already realized close to about INR 600-700 crores ... in April." | FY26 receivables INR 1,485 cr (2.1x on +20% revenue), debtor days 98. WC days 28 → 43. Cash INR 121 → 32 cr. CFO did improve, INR 153 → 277 cr. |
| 12-Aug-26, 30-Oct-26 | Debtors not raised by management. Oct-26 reframed the target as "net working capital days ... in this 90 to 100 days stable region", calling it "best in the industry". (The company itself had quoted NWC days of 62 in Sep-24 and 88 in Dec-24.) | Sep-26 receivables INR 1,223 cr: ~78 days on TTM revenue, ~83 days on annualised H1 |

**How much of the explanation holds up (my own numbers):**
- **The INR 260 cr late receipt:** even after removing it, Mar-26 debtor days are about **80**, not 55.
- **Q4-heavy billing:** this explains part of the rise. On Q4-annualised revenue, debtor days were ~50 (FY25) and ~81 (FY26), or ~67 after removing the INR 260 cr.
- **GST:** this applied in FY25 as well, so it does not explain a year-on-year change.
- **Six months later:** receivables are down only INR 262 cr, and debtor days are still ~25 above the FY25 level.

**Verdict.** The explanation is plausible but incomplete. It came only when asked. The April-2025 promise that working capital would improve was not met: cash flow improved, the receivables cycle did not, and the target was quietly reset.

Other points:
- This does **not** trip the existing kill criterion of debtor days above 120 (`analysis:SKIPPER:2026-11-19`).
- It is the item to watch at Q4FY27.
- Separately, "other asset items" (likely contract assets) rose from INR 232 cr to 400 cr to 455 cr (Mar-25, Mar-26, Sep-26), which is worth splitting out next time.

`insight:marks-calculus-of-value-investcon-2025` | confidence: verified | date: 2025-08-13

Memo of 13 Aug 2025. Observations: about half the S&P 500's 58% two-year return in 2023-24 came from the Magnificent Seven, which reached ~one-third of index value; their average P/E ~33 he did not find unreasonable given 'exceptional products, significant market shares, high incremental profit margins, and strong competitive moats.' But fundamentals looked 'less good overall than they were seven months ago' (tariffs) while prices were higher; S&P +14% in the four months after 1 Apr 2025. A P/E 'is basically the result of applying a discounted cash flow calculation' with inputs growth, durability and ROIC; today's index is faster-growing, less cyclical, less capital-intensive - so 'it's different this time' is a cliche that 'always bears scrutiny' yet failing to see real change 'stands between the average investor and superiority.' Verdict: 'the stock market has moved from "elevated" to "worrisome."' INVESTCON scale: '6. Stop buying; 5. Reduce aggressive holdings and increase defensive holdings; 4. Sell off the remaining aggressive holdings; 3. Trim defensive holdings as well; 2. Eliminate all holdings; 1. Go short.' He says 3-2-1 are essentially never justified ('"overvaluation" is never synonymous with "sure to go down soon"'), and called for INVESTCON 5. Actionable: a graded, reversible response to high temperature - tilt, don't exit.

Sources:
- https://www.oaktreecapital.com/insights/memo/the-calculus-of-value

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:POLYCAB:q3fy27-opm-13pct-plus`
- **Method:** management-tone-vs-delivery · **P(ours)** 0.72 · **P(base)** 0.70 · resolve by 2027-02-28
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 call (Oct-2026): revenue record (+53% YoY per screener: ₹9,899 cr), EBITDA margin 14.4% (+50 bps QoQ); W&C EBIT margin 14.2%; FMEG EBIT 10.1% (first double-digit), FMEG growth +124% (solar). Management keeps the W&C medium-term EBITDA guide at '11% to 13%' and flags 'near-term inflationary pressures… surfacing'. Screener OPM: Sep-24 11.5%, Dec-24 13.8%, Mar-25 14.7%, Jun-25 14.5%, Sep-25 15.8%, Dec-25 12.7%, Mar-26 13.1%, Jun-26 13.8%, Sep-26 14.4%.
- **Why our number differs from base:** Management talks conservatively (11–13% guide) while delivering above it for most quarters — the mirror image of a hype gap. We side with delivery, shaded for copper/inflation and the Q3 FY26 dip to 12.7%.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Persistence: Polycab's screener OPM was ≥13.0% in 7 of the last 9 quarters (~70%).
- **Resolution rule:** YES if Polycab's consolidated Operating Profit ÷ Sales for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 (screener.in quarterly table, or EBITDA ÷ revenue from operations from the results) is ≥13.0%.
- **Resolution source:** Polycab Q3 FY27 results (NSE) / screener.in consolidated quarterly table
- **Sources used:** https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/POLYCAB_19102026163912_Intimation_of_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf; https://www.screener.in/company/POLYCAB/consolidated/
- **Confidence of evidence:** verified
